messages.subject: error dsm.var.gam() from dsm package (dsm_2.2.17)
parts:
Hi there,

I have been getting the following error when estimating the variance of a model with co-variates predicted into new areas:

 model_tw_var_c<- dsm.var.gam(modtw1_ly_df_t_ds_p_h_te2, pred.data = preddata, off.set = off.set)
Error in grad.default(tmfn, ifelse(is.na(eta), 0, eta)) : 
  function returns NA at 0.0003858867257173010.0003377085556092570. and so on.....


I have checked the preddata and there are no NAs indeed, so I am wondering why is this happening? Could you please let me know how I can fix this problem?


Thanks for helping,
Joana

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] error dsm.var.gam() from dsm package (dsm_2.2.17)
parts:
Hi listfolks,

As a follow-up here, this was caused by predicted values that are
numerically zero (i.e., the smallest value that can be represented on
the computer), for which dsm.var.gam can't calculate derivatives, so the
whole procedure falls over.

Removing these (4) observations got around this problem for Joana. They
were found by looking at sort(predict(...))[1:10] and looking at the
smallest values, four of which were 2.220446e-16 (the smallest value on
my machine, found using .Machine$double.eps). The corresponding cells
could then be removed from the prediction grid.

This isn't an ideal solution, so I'll look into a better way to get
around this problem for a future release of dsm. If you have similar
problems in the meantime, please let me know.


cheers,
--dave
